Before anything else

MAYDAY ×3Life in danger
PAN-PAN ×3Urgent, not life-threatening. Ham or GMRS: also “Break, break”

Try 911 first: a phone with no service on your plan can often still reach it. Use the radio when that fails.

2Emergency channelGMRS 20 · 146.520 · see Frequencies

If you hear a distress call

  1. Answer: “Station calling MAYDAY, this is [you]. I hear you. Go ahead.”
  2. Write down location, what happened, how many, needs, time.
  3. Read it back, then call 911 or relay to a repeater, net or anyone with a phone.
  4. Keep the channel clear: “All stations, emergency traffic in progress, please stand by.”

Signal reports (R/S)

How well do I hear you?

RReadability
1Unreadable
2Barely readable, occasional words
3Readable with considerable difficulty
4Readable with practically no difficulty
5Perfectly readable
SStrength
1Faint signals
2Very weak
3Weak
4Fair
5Fairly good
6Good
7Moderately strong
8Strong
9Extremely strong

Give readability first, then strength: “five-nine” = perfectly readable, extremely strong. On FM most people say “loud and clear” (5) or describe it: “readable but scratchy”, “breaking up”.

Emergency

Need help right now?

If anyone's life is in danger, try 911 first: a phone with no service on your own plan can often still reach 911 through any carrier's tower, and text-to-911 works in many areas. Use the radio when that fails.

  1. Stay calm and listen first. Turn the radio on, turn the volume up, and listen on the channel for 10–15 seconds so you don't talk over someone.
  2. Go to an emergency channel. Use the list below, starting with the channel your radio can reach and that people around you are most likely to be listening on.
  3. Turn off privacy codes/tones (CTCSS/DCS, "sub-channels"). Set them to OFF so everyone on the channel can hear you, not just radios with the same code.
  4. Use HIGH power for the emergency call and get high: a hill, a second floor, a rooftop, open ground. Hold the radio straight up, antenna vertical, away from your body and metal.
  5. Press, wait 1 second, speak slowly with the mic 2–3 inches from your mouth. Say the emergency message below, then let go of the button and listen for at least 30 seconds.
  6. Repeat every 1–2 minutes, trying other channels in between. Write down anything you hear. Save battery: listen more than you talk.

Emergency channels to try (in order)

462.675GMRS/FRS Ch 20Widely used as a travel and emergency channel. Many GMRS repeaters on this channel use tone 141.3.
146.520Ham 2 m callingNational simplex calling frequency. Often monitored by hams, especially in disasters.
462.6125FRS/GMRS Ch 3The "3-3-3 plan" channel used by preparedness groups. Also try Ch 1.
446.000Ham 70 cm callingUHF simplex calling frequency.
27.065CB Ch 9 (AM)Official CB emergency channel. CB Ch 19 (27.185) is the trucker/highway channel.
156.800Marine Ch 16Distress and calling on the water. For use on a boat, not on land.
121.500Air "Guard" (AM)Aviation emergency frequency. Listen only on most handhelds and not authorized for ground use.
162.550NOAA WeatherListen for official warnings. Also try 162.400, 162.475, 162.425, 162.450, 162.500 and 162.525.

No frequency is guaranteed to be monitored, and none is a universal emergency channel. Try several, keep calling, and use every other way you have to get help.

Don't know your local repeaters? Before an emergency, save them in Plan → My Radio Book. A repeater on a mountain or tower can carry a handheld 20–50+ miles; simplex (radio to radio) is often 1–5 miles.

What to say

Life-threatening emergency (someone could die or be badly hurt): say "MAYDAY" three times.
Urgent but not life-threatening (stranded, need help soon): say "PAN-PAN" three times, or "Emergency traffic" / "Break, break" on ham or GMRS.

MAYDAY, MAYDAY, MAYDAY. This is [your name / call sign]. My location is [address, road + mile marker, GPS, landmarks]. [What happened: injury / fire / flood / trapped / lost]. [How many people], [their condition]. We need [medical / rescue / water / transport]. Please relay to 911. Over.

Fill in your own details and save them so the script is ready to read: Plan → My emergency message.

If someone answers youHow to pass the message so it gets through
  • Give your location first. If the signal drops, location is what rescuers need most.
  • Spell names and street names with the phonetic alphabet (Learn → Phonetics).
  • Ask them to read it back. Say "read back" and they repeat it to you.
  • Agree on a check-in time and channel ("I'll call back on this channel at 15:00").
  • Numbers: say each digit. "One-two-five" not "a hundred twenty-five." Say "niner" for 9.
  • If you're weak or breaking up, ask a station with a better signal to relay for you.
If you hear someone in distressYou can be the link that saves them
  1. Answer: "Station calling MAYDAY, this is [you]. I hear you. Go ahead."
  2. Write everything down: location, what happened, how many, needs, time.
  3. Read it back to confirm. Then call 911 if you can, or relay to a ham repeater, net or anyone with a phone.
  4. Stay on the channel. Tell other stations to stay off it: "All stations, emergency traffic in progress, please stand by."
The 3-3-3 check-in planFind family and neighbors when phones are down

A simple, widely known schedule: turn your radio on every 3 hours, for at least 3 minutes, on Channel 3. Use local time, at the top of the hour: 12 AM, 3, 6, 9 AM, 12 PM, 3, 6, 9 PM.

Radio"Channel 3"
FRS / GMRS462.6125
MURS151.940
CB26.985
Ham (common)146.520

Don't use privacy codes/sub-channels for this. Many groups also check in every hour (the "1-2-3" idea), and both line up every 3 hours. Agree on your own family's channel and times in advance; it beats any public plan. The countdown to the next window is in Tools.

Other ways to signal for helpWhistle, light, mirror, Morse
  • Three of anything means distress: 3 whistle blasts, 3 flashes, 3 fires in a triangle. Repeat after a pause.
  • SOS in Morse: ··· ––– ··· (3 short, 3 long, 3 short). Use a flashlight, a car horn, or keying the radio on and off.
  • Signal mirror flashes can be seen for miles in sunlight. Aim through a V made with your fingers.
  • Ground signal: a large "SOS" or "X" (X means "need medical help") made of contrasting material in a clearing.
Is it legal to transmit in an emergency?What the rules allow

FCC amateur rules (47 CFR §97.403) let a ham station use any means of radio communication at its disposal when it's needed to protect life or property in an emergency and normal systems aren't available. FRS needs no license at all, and GMRS rules also allow emergency communications.

In practice: a real, immediate threat to life justifies calling on whatever radio and channel will get help. Don't use that to justify everyday use of channels you're not licensed for. And stop once the emergency is over.

I'm not a lawyer; this is a plain-language summary. Get your GMRS license ($35, no exam) and ham Technician license before an emergency so you never have to think about it.

Make the battery lastA radio is useless when it's dead
  • Receiving barely uses power; transmitting uses a lot. Talk briefly, then listen.
  • Use LOW power when the other person is close. Save HIGH for distance.
  • Turn on battery saver (Baofeng Menu 3 SAVE), lower screen brightness, turn off the backlight timer, Bluetooth and dual watch.
  • Don't leave the radio scanning all day. Use a schedule (3-3-3) and turn it off in between.
  • Cold drains lithium batteries. Keep spares in an inside pocket.
  • Carry an AA battery case or a USB-C cable and power bank if your radio supports it (TIDRADIO TD-H3 charges by USB-C).
  • Rough rule: a 2,000–2,500 mAh handheld lasts about a day of light use (5% talk, 5% receive, 90% standby). Use the estimator in Tools.

Program these into every radio today

Do this before you need it. You may not be able to download apps or look things up later.

  • FRS/GMRS 1–22 (preset on GMRS radios) and your local GMRS repeaters
  • NOAA weather channels (preset on most radios)
  • Ham (if licensed): 146.520, 446.000, and your local 2 m and 70 cm repeaters with their tones and offsets
  • Your family's agreed primary and backup channels
  • Airband (on radios that receive AM): 121.5 and your local airport tower, ground and ATIS

GMRS & FRS channel rules in detailPower, bandwidth and repeater channels
  • Ch 1–7 (462.5625–462.7125): FRS 2 W, GMRS up to 5 W.
  • Ch 8–14 (467.5625–467.7125): 0.5 W only, narrowband, both services. Short-range chatter channels.
  • Ch 15–22 (462.550–462.725): FRS 2 W; GMRS up to 50 W. These are also the repeater output channels.
  • Repeater inputs (467.550–467.725) are always 5 MHz above the matching output. Radios label repeater channels "RP15–RP22", "RPT 1–8" or "GMRS-R".
  • Identify with your GMRS call sign (e.g., WSAB123) at the end of a conversation and every 15 minutes during one.
  • FRS and GMRS radios on the same channel can talk to each other.

My emergency plan

Fill this in before you need it. It all stays on this phone; nothing is uploaded. Emergency Mode on the SOS tab reads from it.

Plan readiness
Complete each section below.
1 · How we'll communicate (PACE)Primary, Alternate, Contingency, Emergency

If one method fails, everyone moves to the next. Use the same order for the whole family.

2 · People & contactsFamily, neighbors, out-of-area contact

Pick one out-of-area contact: long-distance calls and texts often get through when local lines are jammed. Everyone checks in with that person.

3 · Meeting pointsWhere we go if we can't talk
4 · Check-in scheduleWhen everyone turns radios on
5 · Home & householdFor your emergency message

Coordinates help rescuers. Read them off a map app while you have service, or a GPS. They also fill in your Maidenhead grid square for ham use.

6 · My emergency messageBuilt from your plan; fill in the rest at the time
7 · My saved channelsStarred from the frequency database

Tap ☆ next to any frequency in the Channels tab to add it here. Starred channels appear in Emergency Mode.

8 · My Radio BookLocal repeaters, nets, airport frequencies, notes

Save local repeaters, airport frequencies, net times and anything else you'll need offline.

NameFreqOffToneNotes
9 · My radiosYour equipment inventory

Serial numbers are optional; if you add them, they stay on this phone only. Model guides are in the Radios tab. Test each radio on the air (a radio check with family or a net) at least every 90 days.

10 · Channel cardA one-page summary to screenshot or print

Builds a clean card from your plan: call sign, PACE methods, saved channels, meeting points and contacts. Screenshot it, print it, and keep a copy with every radio.

11 · Backup: export & importMove your plan to another phone or keep a copy

Privacy: the backup contains names, phone numbers, addresses, medical notes and coordinates in plain text. Store it somewhere private. Don't post it publicly.

        Baofeng6 models · 2 with full guides
        Baofeng UV-5R HamFull guideThe classic budget dual-band
        Bands
        VHF 136–174 MHz, UHF 400–520 MHz (FM only)
        Power
        About 4–5 W high, 1 W low
        Legal use
        Ham bands with a ham license. Not GMRS/FRS/MURS transmit.
        Airband
        No. It can't receive AM aircraft voice.
        Antenna
        Radio has an SMA-male stud → buy SMA-female antennas.
        Program by
        Keypad (menus below) or CHIRP software + USB cable
        UV-5R quick start & tipsCharge, squelch, modes, battery tips

        Quick start

        1. Charge fully in the cradle. Screw the antenna on finger-tight.
        2. Turn the top knob to power on and set volume.
        3. Set squelch (Menu 0) to 3–5.
        4. Press VFO/MR to switch between frequency and channel modes.
        5. Hold # to lock the keypad; hold * to scan.
        6. Before transmitting: confirm you're on a ham frequency and have your call sign ready.

        Tips

        • An aftermarket whip antenna is the cheapest big upgrade.
        • Turn off dual watch (Menu 7) and set battery save (Menu 3) to stretch battery life.
        • Set the transmit time-out (Menu 9) to 60 s so a stuck key doesn't keep transmitting.
        • Check alarm mode (Menu 32) so a long press of CALL doesn't transmit an alarm by accident.

        Faster by computer: Program with CHIRP.

        UV-5R buttonsWhat every key does
        • PTT (big side button): press to talk.
        • CALL (side, top): short press = FM broadcast radio. Long press = alarm. Menu 32 decides if the alarm is a local siren only (SITE) or transmitted (TONE/CODE).
        • MONI (side, bottom): opens squelch to hear weak signals.
        • VFO/MR: switch between Frequency mode (type any frequency) and Channel mode (saved memories).
        • A/B: choose top or bottom line.
        • BAND: switch VHF/UHF in frequency mode.
        • MENU: enter settings and confirm choices. EXIT: back out.
        • ▲ ▼: change channel/frequency or setting.
        • # (hold): lock/unlock the keypad.
        • * (hold): start/stop scanning.
        • Orange light key / flashlight: top-side button on many models.
        UV-5R menu numbersPress MENU, type the number, MENU to change, EXIT
        #NameWhat it does / suggested
        0SQLSquelch level 0–9. Set 3–5. 0 = always open.
        1STEPTuning step. 12.5 K or 25 K is fine for most use.
        2TXPTransmit power HIGH / LOW. Use LOW when close.
        3SAVEBattery saver. Turn ON.
        4VOXVoice-activated transmit. Keep OFF (wastes battery, transmits by accident).
        5WNWide / Narrow bandwidth. WIDE for most ham FM; NARR for narrow channels.
        6ABRBacklight time. Short saves battery.
        7TDRDual watch (listen to A and B). OFF saves battery.
        8BEEPKey beeps on/off.
        9TOTTransmit time-out timer. 60 s prevents a stuck mic.
        10R-DCSReceive DCS code.
        11R-CTCSReceive CTCSS tone. OFF in emergencies so you hear everyone.
        12T-DCSTransmit DCS code.
        13T-CTCSTransmit CTCSS tone. Set the repeater's tone here.
        14VOICEVoice prompts (English/Chinese/off).
        15ANI-IDShows the radio's DTMF ID (view only).
        16DTMFSTDTMF sidetone.
        17S-CODESignal code for DTMF.
        18SC-REVScan resume: TO (time), CO (carrier), SE (search).
        19PTT-IDSends DTMF ID with PTT. Keep OFF.
        20PTT-LTPTT-ID delay.
        21MDF-AChannel display on top line: frequency, channel number or name.
        22MDF-BChannel display on bottom line.
        23BCLBusy channel lockout: blocks transmit when someone is talking.
        24AUTOLKAuto keypad lock.
        25SFT-DOffset direction: OFF / + / −.
        26OFFSETOffset amount, e.g., 00.600 (2 m) or 05.000 (70 cm).
        27MEM-CHSave current frequency to a channel.
        28DEL-CHDelete a channel.
        29WT-LEDStandby screen color.
        30RX-LEDReceive screen color.
        31TX-LEDTransmit screen color.
        32AL-MODAlarm mode: SITE (local siren only), TONE, CODE (transmit).
        33BANDBand for FM broadcast/airband on some models.
        34TDR-ABWhich line transmits when dual watch is on.
        35STESquelch tail elimination.
        36RP-STERepeater squelch tail elimination.
        37RPT-RLRepeater tail delay.
        38PONMSGPower-on message (full screen, voltage, etc.).
        39ROGERRoger beep at end of transmission. OFF is fine.
        40RESETVFO = reset settings only. ALL = also erases channels.
        Program a simplex frequency (UV-5R keypad)Example: 146.520
        1. Press VFO/MR until you see a frequency (not a channel number). Press A/B to use the top line.
        2. Type 146520. Make sure no tones or offsets are set (Menu 13 T-CTCS = OFF, Menu 25 SFT-D = OFF).
        3. Press MENU 2 7 (MEM-CH), press MENU, pick an empty channel number with ▲▼, press MENU, then EXIT.
        4. Optional: press VFO/MR to go to Channel mode, select the channel, then use Menu 21 (MDF-A) to show the frequency or a name.

        If a channel won't save, it may already be used. Delete it with Menu 28 (DEL-CH) and try again.

        Program a repeater (UV-5R keypad)Example: 146.940, −0.600, tone 100.0
        1. Press VFO/MR for Frequency mode, A/B for the top line.
        2. Type the repeater's output frequency: 146940.
        3. MENU 1 3 (T-CTCS) → MENU → choose 100.0 → MENU → EXIT. (This is the tone the repeater needs to hear.)
        4. MENU 2 5 (SFT-D) → MENU → choose − → MENU → EXIT.
        5. MENU 2 6 (OFFSET) → MENU → type 00600 → MENU → EXIT.
        6. MENU 2 7 (MEM-CH) → MENU → choose a channel number → MENU → EXIT.
        7. Test: press VFO/MR to Channel mode, select the channel, key up briefly and say your call sign. You should hear the repeater's "tail" (a short burst of hiss or a beep) after you let go.

        Repeater listings give: output frequency, offset (+/−), and tone (CTCSS/PL). Use Tools → Repeater offset to check the math.

        UV-5R troubleshootingCable, repeater access, noise
        • Cable won't connect: many cheap cables use counterfeit Prolific chips. Use an FTDI-chip cable and push the plug firmly into the radio.
        • Can't hit a repeater: check tone (Menu 13), shift (25) and offset (26).
        • Hear nothing: squelch too high, or a receive tone (Menu 11) is set.
        • Stuck in odd settings: Menu 40 → VFO resets settings but keeps channels.

        Step-by-step checks that work on any radio: no receive audio · can’t reach a repeater · won’t transmit · poor range · programming fails · battery.

        Identification

        Brand
        Baofeng (Pofung). Many look-alike variants exist: UV-5RA, UV-5R Plus, UV-5R Mini, BF-F8HP (BTECH-distributed). Check the exact model on the label.
        Service
        Amateur (ham) transmit with a ham license. Not certified for GMRS, FRS or MURS.

        Specifications

        Memory

        Power
        About 4–5 W high, 1 W low
        Battery
        7.4 V Li-ion, ~1800 mAh standard; desktop cradle
        Antenna
        SMA-male on radio (buy SMA-female antennas)

        Safety & law

        Transmit only within your ham license privileges. The radio will tune GMRS, MURS and marine frequencies, but transmitting there with this radio is not legal (except in a genuine life-threatening emergency). Receiving is fine.

        Baofeng UV-5G / UV-5X GMRSFull guideGMRS-certified cousin of the UV-5R
        UV-5G quick start & programmingFirst call, repeaters, CHIRP model

        Quick start

        1. Charge, attach antenna, power on.
        2. Pick a GMRS channel (1–22) for radio-to-radio. 15–22 have full power.
        3. For a local repeater, use channels 23–30 and set the repeater's tone (by CHIRP or Baofeng's software).
        4. Say your GMRS call sign at the end of a conversation and every 15 minutes.

        Programming

        • CHIRP: choose "Radioddity UV-5G" as the model, not "Baofeng UV-5X" (a different radio).
        • Keypad programming is limited because of GMRS certification; some settings (like tones on some firmware) are easier by computer.
        • Don't use UV-5R menu numbers on this radio without checking its own manual.

        Step by step: Program with CHIRP.

        UV-5G troubleshootingTones, repeaters, CHIRP model
        • Can't change a tone from the keypad: use CHIRP or the Baofeng software.
        • Can't reach a repeater: confirm you're on the matching repeater channel (23–30) with the correct tone.
        • Wrong CHIRP model: upload fails or scrambles settings. Download from the radio first and save a backup.

        Step-by-step checks that work on any radio: no receive audio · can’t reach a repeater · won’t transmit · poor range · programming fails · battery.

        Baofeng GM-15 Pro GMRSHandheld
        GM-15 Pro quick start & controlsFirst call, buttons, modes

        Quick start

        1. Charge the battery fully and attach the antenna.
        2. Never transmit without an antenna (or dummy load) connected.
        3. Turn the volume/power knob clockwise until it clicks; a double beep follows. Turn it the other way to lower volume or switch off.
        4. Set the squelch so the hiss stops, then pick your channel or frequency.
        5. Match the tone (CTCSS/DCS) your group or repeater uses.
        6. Press PTT, wait a moment, then speak across the mic; release to listen.
        7. GMRS: say your call sign at the end of a conversation and at least every 15 minutes.

        Controls

        MENU
        Opens the menu and confirms. Hold in standby to switch between channel and frequency mode.
        Back / WX
        Exits menus and picks the A or B line. Hold 5 seconds to switch between GMRS and NOAA weather.
        Up / Down
        Change channel or frequency (hold to move fast).
        FM / SOS
        Short press: FM radio on/off. Hold 3 seconds: alarm.
        LAMP / Monitor (side)
        Press: flashlight. Hold: monitor (opens squelch). PTT + LAMP sends the repeater access tone.
        ✱ key
        Short press: reverse. Hold 2 seconds: lock or unlock the keypad.

        Channel and frequency mode

        Hold MENU in standby to switch between channel mode (your saved channels) and frequency mode (temporary frequencies, and where you store new channels).

        Written from: Baofeng GM-15 Pro user manual (via RigPix); RigPix GM-15 Pro specifications; Baofeng GM-15 Pro product page.

        GM-15 Pro programmingSave channels, repeaters, reset

        Save a channel

        1. Switch to frequency mode (hold MENU).
        2. Menu 28 (Delete): pick the channel number to clear it first.
        3. Set tones if needed: Menu 10 (RX CTCSS) and Menu 12 (TX CTCSS).
        4. For a repeater: Menu 25 (Direction) and Menu 26 (Offset).
        5. Type the receive frequency on the keypad.
        6. Menu 27 (Memory): pick the channel number to save it.
        7. Hold MENU to go back to channel mode.

        Key lock

        Hold ✱ for over 2 seconds. Menu 24 (AUTO LK) locks the keypad automatically.

        Weather

        Hold Back/WX for 5 seconds, pick one of the 11 weather channels with Up/Down (or hold scan to scan them). Press Back/WX again to leave.

        By computer or app

        Baofeng offers programming software (CPS) and the manual on its GM-15 Pro product page. Names and some codes can only be set with the software. CHIRP support not verified.

        Factory reset

        Menu 40 (RESET): VFO resets menu settings, ALL resets settings and channels.

        Back up first: a factory reset can erase your channels.

        GM-15 Pro troubleshootingFixes from the manual, known quirks
        • Won't turn on: Reseat, recharge or replace the battery; clean dirty contacts.
        • Weak or broken-up receive: Charge the battery, raise the volume, tighten the antenna.
        • Can't reach your group: Match the channel and tones; move closer.
        • Strangers or noise on the channel: Change channel, adjust squelch, or set a tone.
        • Radio keeps transmitting: Turn VOX off and make sure the headset plug is fully seated.

        Good to know

        • Receives broadcast FM and VHF/UHF in addition to GMRS (RigPix lists RX 76–108, 136–174, 400–512 MHz).

        Baofeng UV-9G GMRSHandheld
        UV-9G quick start & controlsFirst call, buttons, modes

        Quick start

        1. Charge the battery fully and attach the antenna.
        2. Never transmit without an antenna (or dummy load) connected.
        3. Turn the volume/power knob clockwise until it clicks; a double beep follows about a second later. Fully counter-clockwise switches it off.
        4. Set the squelch so the hiss stops, then pick your channel or frequency.
        5. Match the tone (CTCSS/DCS) your group or repeater uses.
        6. Press PTT, wait a moment, then speak across the mic; release to listen.
        7. GMRS: say your call sign at the end of a conversation and at least every 15 minutes.

        Controls

        MENU
        Opens the menu, selects items and confirms.
        EXIT
        Leaves the menu / moves the cursor between lines.
        ✱ SCAN
        Hold about 2 seconds to start scanning.
        0 SQL
        Hold about 2 seconds to show battery voltage.
        SOS
        Hold 5 seconds to sound the alarm.
        LED
        Red = transmitting, green = receiving.

        Channel and frequency mode

        With the radio off, hold MENU while turning it on to switch between channel mode (MR, best for everyday use) and frequency mode (VFO, for programming and testing).

        Written from: Baofeng UV-9G user manual (ManualsLib copy); Baofeng UV-9G product pages.

        UV-9G programmingSave channels, repeaters, reset

        Save a channel

        1. Switch to frequency mode (hold MENU while powering on).
        2. Set the tone first: tones can't be changed in channel mode. The manual's example: MENU, 1, 1, MENU, enter the tone (e.g. 123.0), MENU, EXIT.
        3. Type the frequency on the keypad.
        4. Save it: MENU, 2, 7 (memory channel), MENU, type the channel number, then EXIT.
        5. Switch back to channel mode (hold MENU while powering on).

        Key lock

        Covered in the manual; steps not verified here.

        Weather

        Channels 117–127 are the NOAA weather channels; they're fixed and can be scanned and received.

        By computer or app

        Baofeng links its own programming software and CHIRP for the UV-9G. Channel names can only be set with software.

        Factory reset

        Menu 40 (RESET): VFO resets menu settings, ALL resets settings and channels.

        Back up first: a factory reset can erase your channels.

        UV-9G troubleshootingFixes from the manual, known quirks
        • Won't turn on: Reseat the battery, recharge or replace it, and clean the battery contacts.
        • Low-battery icon blinks and it won't transmit: Charge the battery.

        Good to know

        • IP67 rated (Baofeng). Keep the antenna and battery fitted so the seals work.

        UV-5RM / 5RM (2023) quick start & controlsFirst call, buttons, modes

        Quick start

        1. Charge the battery fully and attach the antenna.
        2. Never transmit without an antenna (or dummy load) connected.
        3. Turn the volume knob on top to switch on and set volume.
        4. Set the squelch so the hiss stops, then pick your channel or frequency.
        5. Match the tone (CTCSS/DCS) your group or repeater uses.
        6. Press PTT, wait a moment, then speak across the mic; release to listen.
        7. Ham: say your call sign at least every 10 minutes and at the end.

        Controls

        VFO/MR
        Switches between frequency mode and channel mode.
        Green button (top right)
        Menu / select. In FM radio it changes bands.
        Red button
        Exit / back.
        Top side key
        Short press: FM broadcast radio (then # scans). Long press: flashlight/alarm.
        Bottom side key
        Short press: flashlight. Long press: opens squelch (monitor).
        0 (long press)

        Channel and frequency mode

        Press VFO/MR to move between frequency mode and channel mode.

        Written from: Miklor 5RM review (2023 tri-band).

        UV-5RM / 5RM (2023) programmingSave channels, repeaters, reset

        Save a channel

        1. Press VFO/MR for frequency mode and type the frequency.
        2. Press the green button (menu) and scroll to menu 30 (memory channel).
        3. Press green, pick an empty channel number with the arrows, press green to save.
        4. Press red to leave the menu, then VFO/MR for channel mode.
        5. This is also how to add airband (108–136 MHz) receive channels: the factory software won't accept them.

        Weather

        Long-press 0 for the weather channels; long-press # to scan all 10. A short press returns to the radio.

        By computer or app

        CHIRP (choose model “5RM”) supports everything, including airband channels. The factory software is T6UV (Miklor's software section).

        Not verified yet: key lock, factory reset.

        Back up first: a factory reset can erase your channels.

        UV-5RM / 5RM (2023) troubleshootingFixes from the manual, known quirks
        • Programming error: “check all connections and communication port settings”: Usually the cable isn't fully seated. Push it in firmly; some cables need slight trimming to fit.
        • 220 MHz doesn't work well: The stock antenna doesn't cover 220 MHz; use an antenna made for that band.

        Good to know

        • Miklor measured about 7–8 W on high, 5 W mid, about 2 W low (2 m and 70 cm).
        • The USB-C port only charges the radio; it can't charge other devices.
        • Don't confuse it with the older 2015 dual-band UV-5RM.

        UV-82 family troubleshootingFixes from the manual, known quirks
        • Won't start: Charge or swap the battery; reseat it.

        TIDRADIO TD-H3 GMRS or hamFull guideUSB-C, app programming, airband

        TD-H3 GMRS or Ham version

        Channels
        22 GMRS simplex + 8 repeater, 10 NOAA, 169 programmable
        Receive
        8-band receive including AM airband and FM broadcast
        Charging
        USB-C right on the battery; also a desktop cradle
        Program

        Extras
        Wireless cloning between TD-H3s; "one-key frequency match" copies another radio's frequency
        TD-H3 quick start & tipsFrequency meter, app, cloning, antennas

        Start with Set up a TD-H3, then keep the cheat sheet handy.

        Also have a TD-H3 Plus? The two can’t clone to each other wirelessly. Build one channel list in ODmaster or CHIRP and write it to each radio.

        Tips

        • Hold 1 to use the frequency meter (reads a nearby radio's frequency).
        • Program with the phone app while online, then save the file; wireless cloning copies the setup to other TD-H3s.
        • Use the long antenna only for listening; switch back before transmitting.
        Set up a TIDRADIO TD-H3 (GMRS)From the box to your first call
        1. Charge the battery fully with the USB-C cable or cradle. Swap in the GMRS antenna for talking (the long antenna that comes in the box is for airband listening).
        2. Turn on and use the preset GMRS channels 1–22 to talk radio-to-radio. Ch 15–22 give the most power.
        3. Install the TIDRADIO programming app (called odmaster in reviews) on your phone now, while you have internet. Pair over Bluetooth.
        4. In the app, add local GMRS repeaters: output frequency, +5 MHz offset, and the tone. Name each channel.
        5. Turn on NOAA weather alert if you want warnings while the radio is on.
        6. Add airband channels (receive only): 121.5 and your local airport's tower/ATIS.
        7. Clone the setup to your other TD-H3s wirelessly, so the whole family has the same channel list.
        8. Write the channel list on a card and keep it with the radio (or save it in My Radio Book here).

        Menus differ a little between firmware versions. The app is the easiest way. Keep the paper manual in your go-bag.

        TD-H3 programming cheat sheetGMRS, ham and airband settings at a glance
        WhatReceiveTransmitSettings
        GMRS Ch 1–7462.5625–462.7125sameFM, wide; up to 5 W
        GMRS Ch 8–14467.5625–467.7125sameFM, narrow; 0.5 W max (25 kHz apart)
        GMRS Ch 15–22462.5500–462.7250sameFM, wide; handheld ~5 W (mobiles up to 50 W)
        GMRS repeaters 15R–22R462.550–462.725+5.000 (467.550–467.725)Add the repeater's CTCSS/DCS tone
        Ham simplex146.520 · 146.550 · 146.580 · 146.460 · 446.000 · 446.050 · 446.500FM, no offset, no tone (ham version + license)
        Ham 2 m repeaterslisting±0.600Direction depends on sub-band (see Channels → offsets)
        Ham 70 cm repeaterslisting±5.000Usually + below 445, − above 447
        Airband108–136 (voice 118–136)NoneAM, receive only
        NOAA162.400–162.550NoneFM; Orlando 162.475, Melbourne 162.550

        Airband on the TD-H3

        • The TD-H3 receives 108–136 MHz in AM and can't transmit there. Voice traffic is 118–136; 108–118 is navigation beacons.
        • Use the long airband antenna from the box (often labeled 120/300 MHz or "771"), then switch back to the short GMRS/ham antenna to transmit.
        • Newer firmware handles AM on airband properly. If an active tower frequency gives only hiss, update the firmware or set that channel's mode to AM in the TIDRADIO programming software or CHIRP.
        • Orlando-area tower, ground and ATIS frequencies are in Channels → Central FL.
        TD-H3 troubleshootingAirband hiss, stun code, app
        • Airband is only hiss: update firmware, or set the channel's mode to AM in the software or CHIRP.
        • Radio won't transmit: a stun code can lock the radio to receive-only; check whether one was set in the app.
        • App won't connect: turn Bluetooth on in the radio's settings and keep the phone close.

        TIDRADIO TD-H3 Plus GMRS or hamFull guideThe Bluetooth H3: headsets, app talk, SMS

        TD-H3 Plus GMRS, Ham or Unlocked version

        vs TD-H3
        Same size and functions, plus Bluetooth audio (headsets, wireless PTT, mics), text messages, a spectrum view and app global talk
        Channels
        199 (US ham: 1–188 radio, 189–199 NOAA). GMRS version: 1–54 GMRS only, 55–199 any receive frequency
        Receive
        FM broadcast, AM airband 108–136, VHF, 220, UHF and NOAA
        Program
        ODmaster app or ODmaster Web over Bluetooth, or a cable
        Heads-up
        Won’t clone wirelessly to your original TD-H3
        TD-H3 Plus quick start & tipsFrom the box to your first call

        Quick start

        1. Charge the 2500 mAh battery fully. The USB-C port on the battery only charges; the USB-C port on the radio's side is for programming and updates.
        2. Attach the antenna. Never transmit without one.
        3. Check the mode matches your license: GMRS version for GMRS, Ham version for ham. On firmware 1.0.37 and later, holding PTT1 + ✱ while switching on picks GMRS, Ham or Normal mode.
        4. Switch on, set volume, and press V/M to use your channels.
        5. Install ODmaster on your phone now, while you have internet. Pair from inside the app, not from the phone's Bluetooth settings.
        6. Load the same channel list you use on your TD-H3 (app, ODmaster Web or CHIRP). Wireless cloning between the H3 and the H3 Plus doesn't work.
        7. Update the firmware while you're online (see “Update the firmware”).
        8. Talk: press PTT, wait a moment, speak; release to listen. Give your call sign (GMRS every 15 minutes and at the end; ham every 10 minutes and at the end).

        Tips

        • Two PTT buttons: the upper one transmits on display A, the lower one on display B.
        • Long-press 1 to copy a nearby radio's frequency and tone, then press MENU to save it. Repeater offsets must be added by hand.
        • Long-press 0 for NOAA weather; long-press 5 to swap receive/transmit (hear a repeater's input directly).
        • Channel names can be up to 8 characters.
        • Bluetooth audio has a slight delay compared with the radio's own speaker (a reviewer's note).
        TD-H3 Plus buttons & shortcutsWhat each key does
        MENU (blue)
        Open the menu and confirm. Long press: Bluetooth on/off.
        V/M (orange)
        Switch frequency mode and channel mode.
        #
        Switch between A and B.
        ✱ (long)
        Lock / unlock the keypad.
        1 (long)
        Frequency capture: copies a nearby transmitter's frequency and tone.
        5 (long)
        Reverse (swap RX and TX).
        0 (long)
        NOAA weather mode.
        Upper / lower PTT
        Transmit on A / on B.
        PF1 / PF2 (side)
        Short and long press set in Menu → Radio Setting (FM radio, lamp, monitor, tone, alarm, weather, PTT2, OD PTT). PF1 becomes the ODmaster PTT while Bluetooth is connected.
        Top key
        Alarm.

        Key functions are from firmware 1.0.45 and Miklor's review. Menus can change with firmware updates.

        TD-H3 Plus Bluetooth: headset, PTT, phone & appPair accessories and ODmaster

        Headset, earbuds or wireless PTT

        1. Long-press MENU to turn Bluetooth on.
        2. In the Bluetooth menu, set the radio to Emitter mode (the radio connects to the accessory).
        3. Put the headset or PTT button in pairing mode and search from the radio.
        4. Pick it from the list; the radio shows “Conn success”.

        Bluetooth menus 7–10 adjust the mic and speaker level for Bluetooth audio.

        ODmaster app (programming and talk)

        1. Turn Bluetooth on (long-press MENU).
        2. Open ODmaster and pair from inside the app. Don't pair in the phone's settings.
        3. Edit channels in the app, or at web.odmaster.net on a computer; the list syncs to the phone and writes to the radio over Bluetooth.
        4. ODmaster PTT has two modes: OD (app only, over the internet) and OD + Analog (internet and radio together).

        App “global talk” and group calls need the internet and phone networks. In a real outage, plan on radio-to-radio (simplex) and repeaters.

        TD-H3 Plus program channels & repeatersCapture, app, cable, CHIRP

        Fastest: copy another radio

        1. Long-press 1.
        2. Have the other radio transmit.
        3. The screen shows the frequency and tone; press MENU to save it to a channel.
        4. For a repeater, add the offset afterward (GMRS: +5 MHz; 2 m ham: ±0.6 MHz; 70 cm: ±5 MHz).

        Easiest for a full list: ODmaster

        Build the list once in ODmaster Web or the app and write it over Bluetooth. Keep a saved copy for your TD-H3 too.

        By cable

        Use the side USB-C port, or a K1-plug cable with a UART chip in the USB end (drivers usually install automatically). TIDRADIO's factory software is on its support portal.

        CHIRP

        An owner reports CHIRP's TD-H3 Plus driver is experimental with minor bugs. ODmaster is the safer choice.

        Channel layout

        US ham version: channels 1–188 for radio and airband, 189–199 NOAA. GMRS version: 1–54 GMRS only, 55–199 any receive frequency.

        TD-H3 Plus update the firmwareDo it while you have internet
        1. Easiest: ODmaster Web in Chrome on a computer: Remote Control Program → Firmware Upgrade (TIDRADIO says no software install is needed).
        2. USB-C method (firmware 1.0.26 or later): connect the radio's side USB-C port, hold PTT + 3 while switching on, run TIDRADIO's updater and pick the .fw file.
        3. K-plug method: hold PTT + 1 while switching on and use TIDRADIO's updater with a CH340 K-plug cable.
        4. After updating, check the version in the menu and test transmit on both A and B.

        One owner's USB-C update didn't work and the K-plug method did. Follow TIDRADIO's current instructions for your firmware.

        TD-H3 Plus troubleshootingBluetooth, app, SMS, cloning, updates
        • Can't connect a Bluetooth headset or PTT: make sure the radio is in Emitter mode and the accessory is in pairing mode.
        • App can't find the radio: turn Bluetooth on (long-press MENU) and pair inside ODmaster, not in phone settings.
        • Won't clone to my TD-H3: normal. Wireless cloning only works between two H3 Plus radios; program the TD-H3 separately.
        • Computer won't see the radio: use the side USB-C port; the battery's USB-C port only charges.
        • Text messages missed: SMS reception is more reliable with Dual Watch (Menu 10) off.
        • FM broadcast keeps playing: when a side key starts FM radio, it stays on until there's activity on your channel, then returns about 5 seconds after the signal drops.
        • Odd behavior after an update: menus change between firmware versions (for example the modulation setting). Check the version and TIDRADIO's notes.
        • Airband is just hiss: airband is receive-only AM (108–136 MHz); use a longer antenna for listening.

        Yaesu5 models
        Yaesu FT-65R HamHandheld
        FT-65R quick start & controlsFirst call, buttons, modes

        Quick start

        1. Charge the battery fully and attach the antenna.
        2. Never transmit without an antenna (or dummy load) connected.
        3. Turn PWR/VOL out of its click-stop to switch on (battery voltage shows for 2 seconds); turn it to set volume; fully counter-clockwise switches off.
        4. Set the squelch so the hiss stops, then pick your channel or frequency.
        5. Match the tone (CTCSS/DCS) your group or repeater uses.
        6. Press PTT, wait a moment, then speak across the mic; release to listen.
        7. Ham: say your call sign at least every 10 minutes and at the end.

        Controls

        V/M
        Switch between frequency (VFO) and memory mode. Hold to store a memory.
        #BAND
        Cycles 144 MHz, 430 MHz and FM broadcast.
        F
        Press before a key for its second function; hold to enter Set Mode.
        MONI/T.CALL
        Opens squelch (US version).
        P1–P4
        Hold to store a favorite setup; press to recall. F+P1 = Home channel, F+P2 = power.
        1 (hold)
        Weather channels.
        6 (hold)
        Key lock.
        ▲ / ▼
        Tune; hold to scan.

        Channel and frequency mode

        Press V/M to switch. In memory mode use ▲/▼ or type the channel number.

        Written from: Yaesu FT-65R/E Operating Manual (via RigPix).

        FT-65R programmingSave channels, repeaters, reset

        Save a channel

        1. In VFO mode set the frequency, tone, shift and power.
        2. Hold V/M: a blank channel appears (change it with ▲/▼ if you like).
        3. Optional: type a name on the keypad (F moves the cursor).
        4. Hold V/M again: “MEM-IN” blinks and a tone sounds.
        5. Repeater shift is automatic (ARS) in the repeater sub-bands (0.6 MHz on 2 m). Manual: hold F → 24 REPEATER → MODE → +REP/−REP, then SHIFT; PTT saves.
        6. Squelch: F, then MONI/T.CALL → set with ▲/▼ → PTT to save.

        Key lock

        Hold 6. Set Mode item 15 chooses keypad, PTT, or both.

        Weather

        Hold 1 for the weather channels.

        By computer or app

        Optional SCU-35 programming cable with Yaesu's PC software; SCU-36 for radio-to-radio cloning.

        Factory reset

        Power off. Hold MONI/T.CALL + PTT and power on; release when the backlight comes on. Pick F1 SET RESET, F2 MEM RESET, F3 BANK RESET or F4 ALL RESET with ▲/▼, then press F.

        Back up first: a factory reset can erase your channels.

        FT-65R troubleshootingFixes from the manual, known quirks
        • Won't power on: Check the battery charge and that it's seated.
        • No sound: Squelch too high, volume too low, or tone squelch / DCS turned on.
        • Won't transmit: Check PTT lock, busy-channel lockout, that you're not on FM broadcast, and battery voltage.
        • Keys don't respond: Keypad or PTT lock is on.
        • “Charging Error”: Use a Yaesu charger; the pack may be over-discharged or worn out.

        Good to know

        • IP54: splash and dust resistant only with the antenna, battery and jack cap fitted. Never submerge it.

        Step-by-step checks that work on any radio: no receive audio · can’t reach a repeater · won’t transmit · poor range · programming fails · battery.

        Yaesu FT-70DR HamHandheld
        FT-70DR quick start & controlsFirst call, buttons, modes

        Quick start

        1. Charge the battery fully and attach the antenna.
        2. Never transmit without an antenna (or dummy load) connected.
        3. Hold the POWER (LOCK) switch to switch on/off; turn the volume knob.
        4. Set the squelch so the hiss stops, then pick your channel or frequency.
        5. Match the tone (CTCSS/DCS) your group or repeater uses.
        6. Press PTT, wait a moment, then speak across the mic; release to listen.
        7. Ham: say your call sign at least every 10 minutes and at the end.

        Controls

        V/M (DW)
        Switch VFO / memory. Hold to start a memory write.
        AMS
        Mode select: AMS auto, TX FM or TX digital.
        BAND
        Next band up.
        MODE
        Receive mode.
        F
        Second function of the next key.
        GM
        Group Monitor on/off.
        HM/RV
        Home channel / reverse.

        Channel and frequency mode

        Press V/M to switch between VFO and memory. Holding V/M while switching on starts “memory channel only” mode.

        Written from: Yaesu FT-70DR Operating and Advance Manuals (ManualsLib/RigPix copies); Yaesu FT-70DR product page (ADMS-10).

        FT-70DR programmingSave channels, repeaters, reset

        Save a channel

        1. Set the frequency and mode you want to save.
        2. Hold V/M; the memory number blinks.
        3. Turn the DIAL to the channel (empty channels blink).
        4. Press V/M to save; you can add a 6-character name (Set Mode 33 MEM.NAM).
        5. Clear a memory: V/M, hold V/M, pick it with the DIAL, press AMS twice (“M-MSK?”).
        6. Banks: up to 24 (b1–b24); F then BAND opens them.

        Key lock

        POWER (LOCK) switch.

        By computer or app

        Yaesu ADMS-10 programming software (free from Yaesu) with a programming cable.

        Factory reset

        All Reset (erases memories): power off, hold MODE + HM/RV + AMS while switching on. Settings only: hold MODE + V/M while switching on.

        Back up first: a factory reset can erase your channels.

        FT-70DR troubleshootingFixes from the manual, known quirks
        • ADMS-10 can't talk to the radio: Check the cable is fully in the data port and the PC; charge or replace the battery.

        Good to know

        • AMS switches automatically between FM and C4FM digital to match the other station.
        • AM airband receive is built in (108–137 MHz).

        Save a channel

        1. 207 memory channels (including 6 scan-edge channels and 1 Call channel). Each stores frequency, width, duplex direction with offset, and tones.
        2. Copy a memory to another memory: pick memory mode, FUNC then VFO/MR/CALL (X and -- blink), pick the target with ▲/▼, then FUNC and hold VFO/MR/CALL for 1 second.
        3. Clear a memory: memory mode, FUNC then VFO/MR/CALL, pick it with ▲/▼, then confirm within 1.5 seconds as the manual shows.
        4. US version: Auto Repeater sets the duplex direction and tone automatically inside the repeater sub-band.

        Key lock

        FUNC, then hold the lock key for 1 second (see the manual).

        Weather

        US version: 10 NOAA weather channels; press VFO/MR/CALL until weather mode shows.

        By computer or app

        Optional CS-V86 software with the OPC-474 cable (also clones radio to radio through the speaker jacks).

        Factory reset

        All reset: power off, hold MONI + VFO/MR/CALL and hold power for 1 second. “CLEAR” shows. Erases all programming.

        Back up first: a factory reset can erase your channels.

        IC-V86 troubleshootingFixes from the manual, known quirks
        • No power: Charge or replace the battery, check polarity, clean the terminals.
        • No sound: Turn VOL up; unplug an external speaker or programming cable from the SP jack.
        • Won't transmit: Charge the battery; set “TX permission” ON in Set mode; turn Lockout off.
        • VOX won't transmit: Raise VOX gain and mic gain; check TX permission.
        • Can't talk to another station directly: Different tone or DTCS code; use tone scan to find it.
        • Can't set a frequency: Cancel key lock; switch to VFO mode.
        • Memory scan won't start: Switch to memory mode; program at least 2 memories.
        • Display shows nonsense: Reset the CPU, or remove and refit the battery.

        Good to know

        • 7 W and 1500 mW of audio (Icom). Analog FM only.

        Step-by-step checks that work on any radio: no receive audio · can’t reach a repeater · won’t transmit · poor range · programming fails · battery.

        Icom IC-705 HamPortable HF/VHF/UHF
        IC-705 quick start & controlsFirst call, buttons, modes

        Quick start

        1. Connect it to a proper 13.8 V DC supply or the vehicle battery with the fused cable, and mount it securely.
        2. Never transmit without an antenna (or dummy load) connected.
        3. Runs on its battery pack or external DC; full 10 W needs external DC (see manual).
        4. Set the squelch so the hiss stops, then pick your channel or frequency.
        5. Match the tone (CTCSS/DCS) your group or repeater uses.
        6. Press PTT, wait a moment, then speak across the mic; release to listen.
        7. Ham: say your call sign at least every 10 minutes and at the end.

        Controls

        Touch screen
        Most settings: MENU → SET.
        MW (touch, hold 1 s)
        Writes the current settings into the selected memory.

        Channel and frequency mode

        VFO and memory; changes made while in memory mode aren't saved until you write them.

        Written from: Icom IC-705 Basic Manual (ManualsLib copy); ARRL QST IC-705 review.

        IC-705 programmingSave channels, repeaters, reset

        Save a channel

        1. To save changes to a memory: on the VFO/MEMORY screen touch MW for 1 second.
        2. Back up settings and memories to the microSD card (SET → SD Card → Save Setting) before resets or updates.

        Weather

        US version has weather channel operation.

        By computer or app

        Firmware updates from microSD (copy the file into the card's IC-705 folder).

        Factory reset

        MENU → SET → Others → Reset → Partial Reset (keeps memories, call signs, repeater list, Wi-Fi) or All Reset (erases everything; touch NEXT, then YES).

        Not verified yet: key lock.

        Back up first: a factory reset can erase your channels.

        IC-705 troubleshootingFixes from the manual, known quirks
        • Memory didn't keep my changes: Touch MW for 1 second to overwrite it.
        • “OVF” on screen: Signal too strong: lower RF gain, turn on the attenuator, turn off the preamp.
        • Scope only shows strong signals: Raise the reference level.
        • Voice memories won't transmit: Set “DATA OFF MOD” back to MIC,USB (or MIC).
        • “No SD Card is found”: Reinsert or replace the microSD card.
        • “– No File –” on Firmware Update: Put the file in the IC-705 folder, re-download it, or format the card.
        • Touch screen off target: Calibrate it on the OTHERS screen.
        • Clock resets: Connect power so the clock's backup battery charges.

        Good to know

        • No built-in antenna tuner: use a resonant antenna or an external tuner (ARRL review).

        Step-by-step checks that work on any radio: no receive audio · can’t reach a repeater · won’t transmit · poor range · programming fails · battery.

        Quick start

        1. Charge the battery fully and attach the antenna.
        2. Never transmit without an antenna (or dummy load) connected.
        3. Turn the volume knob to switch on and set volume.
        4. Set the squelch so the hiss stops, then pick your channel or frequency.
        5. Match the tone (CTCSS/DCS) your group or repeater uses.
        6. Press PTT, wait a moment, then speak across the mic; release to listen.
        7. GMRS: say your call sign at the end of a conversation and at least every 15 minutes.

        Controls

        Channel knob / ▲▼
        Scroll channels.
        MENU
        Open menus and confirm.
        EXIT
        Back to standby; hold for a quick guide to the side keys.
        AREA
        Switch dual-display areas A and B (dual display is off by default).
        PF1 / PF2
        Programmable short/long press (e.g. flashlight).

        Channel and frequency mode

        Channel mode for saved channels; frequency mode tunes anything in the receive range but only transmits on GMRS.

        KG-935G Plus programmingSave channels, repeaters, reset

        Save a channel

        1. Add or delete channels: menu 42 (CH-ADD) and 43 (CH-DELETE), from frequency mode or by cloning an existing channel.
        2. Channel Wizard (menu 61) loads the current channel; edit it and choose SAVE END or SAVE NEW.
        3. Repeaters: RPT-15 to RPT-22 receive on GMRS 15–22 and transmit on 467 MHz; menu 54 (REPEATER) lets you use a repeater from frequency mode.

        Key lock

        When on, everything except ✱LOCK and PTT is disabled, including the channel knob.

        Weather

        Weather Alert (menu 07) watches NOAA in standby; menu 23 sets how you're alerted. Find your station at weather.gov/nwr.

        By computer or app

        Wouxun software with the PCO-001 cable, or RT Systems. CHIRP supports the KG-935G (Buy Two Way Radios, Nov 2022); check CHIRP's list for the Plus.

        Menu 62 (RESET) → ALL resets settings and channels. Often fixes odd behavior.

        Back up first: a factory reset can erase your channels.

        BTECH3 models
        BTECH GMRS-V2 GMRSHandheld
        GMRS-V2 quick start & controlsFirst call, buttons, modes

        Quick start

        1. Charge the battery fully and attach the antenna.
        2. Never transmit without an antenna (or dummy load) connected.
        3. Turn the volume/power knob clockwise until it clicks; two beeps, then the channel shows. Turning too far down switches it off. Hold M to open squelch while you set volume.
        4. Set the squelch so the hiss stops, then pick your channel or frequency.
        5. Match the tone (CTCSS/DCS) your group or repeater uses.
        6. Press PTT, wait a moment, then speak across the mic; release to listen.
        7. GMRS: say your call sign at the end of a conversation and at least every 15 minutes.

        Controls

        PTT rocker
        Press up to talk on the top line (A), down for the bottom line (B).
        Side key 1 [F]
        Short: FM broadcast radio. Hold: alarm. Press while holding PTT: tone burst.
        Side key 2 [M]
        Short: flashlight. Hold: monitor.
        #
        Short: high/low power. Hold: keypad lock.
        ✱
        Short: reverse. Hold: scan.
        0
        Hold: battery voltage.
        MENU / EXIT
        Enter and confirm / cancel; EXIT also switches between A and B.

        Channel and frequency mode

        Channel mode is the main mode (GMRS, scanner and NOAA channels). Frequency mode lets you tune or type frequencies but only receives there; store new frequencies to memory from frequency mode.

        Written from: BTECH GMRS-V2 user manual; BTECH software page (CHIRP model name).

        GMRS-V2 programmingSave channels, repeaters, reset

        Save a channel

        1. Receive-only channel: in frequency mode set the frequency, Menu 27 (RCH-AD), pick an empty memory (000–199), confirm.
        2. GMRS channel: Menu 43 (GCH-AD), pick a memory, type the GMRS channel number.
        3. Weather channel: Menu 44 (NCH-AD), pick a memory, type the NOAA channel (01–07).
        4. Tones: Menu 11 (RX CTCSS) and 13 (TX CTCSS); DCS is Menu 10 and 12. Set both the same, or OFF.

        Key lock

        Hold # for about 2 seconds. Side keys still work.

        Weather

        Add a weather channel with Menu 44, then pick it like any channel.

        By computer or app

        BTECH's GMRS-V2 Windows software, or CHIRP-next (model “BTECH GMRS-V2”). A PC cable is sold separately. Renaming channels needs software.

        Factory reset

        Menu 45 (RESET): VFO or ALL. Restores the default 30 GMRS channels.

        Back up first: a factory reset can erase your channels.

        GMRS-V2 troubleshootingFixes from the manual, known quirks
        • Won't power on: Recharge or replace the battery; reseat it.
        • Battery drains fast: Charge fully; replace a weak battery.
        • Light shows a signal but no sound: Raise the volume; match or turn off CTCSS/DCS.
        • Others can't hear you: Match CTCSS/DCS; move closer.
        • Transmits without PTT: Turn VOX off or lower its sensitivity.
        • Can't hear others: Match tones; press M while they talk to check.

        BTECH GMRS-PRO GMRSHandheld
        GMRS-PRO quick start & controlsFirst call, buttons, modes

        Quick start

        1. Charge the battery fully and attach the antenna.
        2. Never transmit without an antenna (or dummy load) connected.
        3. Turn the top knob clockwise to switch on; turn it to set volume, fully counter-clockwise to switch off.
        4. Set the squelch so the hiss stops, then pick your channel or frequency.
        5. Match the tone (CTCSS/DCS) your group or repeater uses.
        6. Press PTT, wait a moment, then speak across the mic; release to listen.
        7. GMRS: say your call sign at the end of a conversation and at least every 15 minutes.

        Controls

        Up / Down
        Page up/down.
        OK
        Open items and confirm.
        Menu
        Opens the menu.
        Back
        Back out of menus; on the main screen it cycles three screen layouts.
        Exit / Lock (red)
        Exit to the main screen. Long press: lock/unlock keys (PTT still works).
        P1 (orange), P2, P3
        Shortcuts you set in the app. P1 pressed twice (or held 2 s) starts Bluetooth pairing.

        Channel and frequency mode

        Channels are in groups: group 1 holds the GMRS channels and can't be changed; groups 2–6 are yours. Pick the group in Radio Settings → Channel Group.

        Written from: BTECH GMRS-PRO user manual; BTECH software page.

        GMRS-PRO programmingSave channels, repeaters, reset

        Save a channel

        1. App (easiest): open BTECH GMRS Programmer, pair inside the app (not in phone Bluetooth settings), long-press a channel square, edit name, frequencies, tones, power and bandwidth, then save.
        2. Receive-only channel: set the transmit frequency to 0.
        3. Repeater: set the repeater's transmit/receive pair and tone; Talk Around makes TX equal RX.
        4. On the radio: Menu → Edit Frequency / Memory Settings. New frequencies only go in groups 2–6.

        Key lock

        Long-press the red Exit/Lock key.

        Weather

        WX Mode: Off, Monitor or Alert. Pick your local channel under WX Channel. Alerts sound for NOAA warnings; press any key to mute.

        By computer or app

        BTECH GMRS Programmer app (iPhone, Android) over Bluetooth. No cable or desktop software needed.

        Factory reset

        Hold P1 + P2 together in standby (erases your settings; back up in the app first). The menu also has Reset Settings and Factory Data Reset.

        Back up first: a factory reset can erase your channels.

        GMRS-PRO troubleshootingFixes from the manual, known quirks
        • Screen stays dark after a firmware update: Hold P1 + P2 to restore factory settings.
        • Volume knob does nothing with a wireless mic or earphone: Set Speaker to Off or Auto.
        • Compass shows = or 8: Calibrate: level and screen up (=), or draw a figure-8 in the air (8). Keep away from magnets.
        • Audio feedback squeal: Turn off Audio Relay, especially with radios close together.
        • Battery dies early or in the cold: Replace an aged battery; keep a spare warm.
        • Bluetooth headset won't transmit: You need a Bluetooth PTT button.

        Good to know

        • Text messages: Signaling → Send Message. Channels 23–30 can't send data.
        • Location: turn on Position to share yours; Allow Check lets partners request it.
        • The earphone jack is proprietary, not a standard plug.

        BTECH UV-50X2 (2nd gen) HamMobile
        UV-50X2 (2nd gen) quick start & controlsFirst call, buttons, modes

        Quick start

        1. Connect it to a proper 13.8 V DC supply or the vehicle battery with the fused cable, and mount it securely.
        2. Never transmit without an antenna (or dummy load) connected.
        3. Push and hold the volume knob to switch on or off. Turn it to set volume. Press the Confirm key (main selector) to turn squelch on/off; Menu 2 sets the level 0–9.
        4. Set the squelch so the hiss stops, then pick your channel or frequency.
        5. Match the tone (CTCSS/DCS) your group or repeater uses.
        6. Press PTT, wait a moment, then speak across the mic; release to listen.
        7. Ham: say your call sign at least every 10 minutes and at the end.

        Controls

        V/M
        Switch channel and frequency mode (or long-press MENU on the mic).
        Confirm / main selector
        Confirm menu choices, change settings.
        Monitor
        Opens squelch.
        FM
        FM broadcast radio.
        Call
        Sends caller ID / selected signaling.
        Exit
        Leave menus, switch A/B/C/D lines, alarm.
        High/Low
        Power level; hold to lock keys.
        Mic ✱/SCAN, #/LOCK, 0–9
        Scan; power (hold: lock); number entry.

        Channel and frequency mode

        Frequency mode for testing and entering data before saving; channel mode for saved channels. The change applies only to the selected line (A/B/C/D).

        Written from: BTECH 2nd-gen UV-25X2/25X4/50X2 manual; BTECH software page (CHIRP model name); Miklor UV-50X2 review.

        UV-50X2 (2nd gen) programmingSave channels, repeaters, reset

        Save a channel

        Example from the manual (channel 99, RX 145.000, TX 145.600, tone 123.0):

        1. V/M to frequency mode. Menu 45 (DEL-CH) → 99 to clear the channel.
        2. Menu 13 (T-CTCS) → 123.0.
        3. Type 145000, then Menu 44 (MEM-CH) → 99 (saves receive).
        4. Type 145600, then Menu 44 (MEM-CH) → 99 (saves transmit).
        5. V/M back to channel mode. Channels store the transmit frequency, not an offset.

        Key lock

        Hold # about 2 seconds. Menu 4 (AUTOLK) locks after 8 seconds idle.

        By computer or app

        BTECH UV-50X2 Windows software (2nd-gen package) with the PC-04 cable in the DATA jack, or CHIRP-next (model “BTECH UV-50X2_G2”).

        Factory reset

        Menu 62 (RESET): VFO or ALL (ALL deletes channels).

        Back up first: a factory reset can erase your channels.

        UV-50X2 (2nd gen) troubleshootingFixes from the manual, known quirks
        • Smoke or a hot smell: Cut power immediately and send it for service.
        • Can't use a repeater: Recheck frequency, offset and tone; ask the repeater owner or local club.
        • High SWR: Use an antenna at 1.5:1 or better. Never transmit without an antenna or dummy load.

        Good to know

        • Power: 13.8 V DC (±15%), up to 20 A peak, through the direct-connect cable with its fuse. Never 24 V.
        • At 50 W it draws about 10–13 A, so wire it to the battery or a fuse block, not a lighter socket (Miklor).
        • Don't mount it over an airbag.

        DB20-G quick start & controlsFirst call, buttons, modes

        Quick start

        6. Press PTT, wait a moment, then speak across the mic; release to listen.

        Number keys (mic)
        Type a channel number directly (001 = channel 1).
        Up / Down (mic)
        Change channel.
        PTT
        Hold to talk.

        Switches frequency and channel mode.

        Channel and frequency mode

        Step size and FM radio work only in frequency mode; channel names and channel scan work in channel mode.

        DB20-G programmingSave channels, repeaters, reset

        Save a channel

        1. Tones: menus 01–03 set CTCSS/DCS (the mic's 1 key picks the code type inside the menu).
        2. Repeater channels RPT-1 to RPT-8 are built in (462.x receive / 467.x transmit); 9 extra repeater channels can be programmed.
        3. Mic-by-mic repeater entry isn't spelled out in the manual; the computer is the reliable way.

        Key lock

        Hold the lock key until LOCK shows; hold again (two beeps) to unlock.

        Weather

        7 NOAA channels (Radioddity).

        By computer or app

        Radioddity's DB20-G software with the USB cable (install the USB-to-COM driver first); the programming port shares the mic jack. Radioddity also lists CHIRP.

        Factory reset

        Menu 30 (RESTORE): FACTORY resets settings; INITIALIZE resets settings and channels (the manual is inconsistent on which clears channels). Hold the key until it restarts.

        Back up first: a factory reset can erase your channels.

        DB20-G troubleshootingFixes from the manual, known quirks
        • Signal bars flash but no sound: A matching carrier with different tones. Check CTCSS/DCS.
        • Behaves oddly after setting changes: Do a factory reset (Menu 30).
        • Won't transmit on channels 8–14: Normal: those are 0.5 W FRS channels and this radio's minimum is 5 W.

        Good to know

        • Power: 12–14 V DC, 10 A or more. Fuse: 10 A (included).
        • Antenna: SL16 / SO-239 (UHF) connector, rated 20 W or more.
